newsitem.title: INDIA: India likely to woo private funding for state TV.
newsitem.headline: India likely to woo private funding for state TV.

text.p: India's cabinet will be asked to rule on private investment in one of the country's state-run television channels, officials at the Information and Broadcasting Ministry said on Wednesday.

The officials told Reuters that the investment in the Doordarshan 3 (DD3) channel, if approved, would total about three billion rupees ($84 million) and cover 30 transmitters across the country. The officials did not detail a time-frame for the submission to the cabinet.

The state-run DD 3, dubbed an "elitist" channel because of its mainly cultural and current-affairs fare, has been running at a loss since it was launched in September 1995, information ministry officials said.

"The fact is that we will be going to the cabinet to seek the approval if in some way private investment can be attracted for setting up transmitters for DD 3 to make it a terrestrial channel," the officials said. "We will try to explore the possibilities once we get the go-ahead from the cabinet."
If the cabinet approves the move, tenders will most likely be floated to invite private investment, they said.

Media tycoon Kerry Packer, who runs Australia's Channel 9 sports channel, Subash Chandra of Zee TV, India's most successful private cable channel, and Malaysia's Measat "have shown interest in some kind of partnership with DD3", the officials said.
